newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare gains on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare gains on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed firmer but below-session highs Monday as dealers took profits at the end of a quiet day.
Trading was light because U.S. banks were closed for Veterans Day.
"Some dealers took profits prior to the close. Volume was reasonable, but it was not not an active session," said a trader.
The leading IPC index closed up 22.06 points, or 0.66 percent, at 3,369.72. Volume was 85.1 million shares traded.
On the broad market, of a total of 110 stocks traded, with gainers outnumbering losers by 61 to 26.

Situr, part of the debt-ridden Sidek group, gained 7 centavos (1 cent) to 68 centavos (9 cents) to head the gainers after a technical rebound, but traders noted the stock was well below its year high of 3.12 pesos (39 cents).
Financial stock GFInver was also a notable gainer, with CCP series closing up 6 centavos (1 cent) at 63 centavos (8 cents). Traders said dealers bought GFInver stock on speculation
over the subscription price of a new share issue to help finance its forthcoming acquisition by Banco Santander.
"Dealers think the subscription price will be 51 centavos per share," said a trader, referring to the mooted GFInver share offer.

Traders also noted that blue-chip construction stock ICA benefited from upgrading on Monday by UBS Securities and Robert Fleming Research. ICA gained 2.90 pesos (37 cents) to close at 110.00 pesos ($13.92)
Financial stock GFSerfin headed the losers, falling 20 centavos (3 cents) to 3.60 pesos (46 cents) on thin volume.
Equity analysts, meanwhile, said the market was still on a short-term upward trend.

"We're still within an upside trend. Potentially unsettling domestic and foreign events are behind us now. The only one left in the short term is the (U.S.) Federal Open Market Committee meeting (on Wednesday), but the market has already discounted any change in rates," said Roberto Galvan, analyst at consultant Bursametrica.
